name: N,n-dimethylbenzylamine
description: N,N-Dimethylbenzylamine (CAS 103-83-3 ), commonly known as BDMA, is a tertiary amine used primarily as a catalyst and curing accelerator in industrial chemical processes. It functions as a reactive intermediate and process accelerator across polymer, coatings, and specialty chemical manufacturing. In epoxy resin systems, BDMA acts as a curing accelerator and hardener catalyst, shortening cure cycles in adhesives, coatings, and composite manufacturing. Formulators in polyurethane production use it to catalyze foam formation and control reaction rates. In flavor and fragrance applications, it serves as a chemical intermediate for synthesizing quaternary ammonium compounds and other nitrogen-based actives used in preservation and biocidal formulations. It is a versatile component for many industrial sectors. Biotechnology and life sciences manufacturers also source BDMA as a synthesis building block for producing specialty reagents and active pharmaceutical intermediates. Its chemical structure allows for precise control in complex organic synthesis pathways. N,N-Dimethylbenzylamine is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in standard drum and IBC packaging suited for industrial volumes. Technical grade is the predominant commercial specification for most large-scale manufacturing needs. Purity levels are typically at 99% or higher for catalyst-grade applications. Buyers requiring tighter specifications for pharmaceutical intermediate use should confirm supplier documentation against relevant compendial or internal quality standards. The material is handled according to strict safety protocols to ensure stability and performance in sensitive chemical reactions.
